title: The Figure the Counter Asks For on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement
content:
## The quantity to be arrived at

What the guest is asked to hand over at the counter on a rental agreement of the Equipment Rental and Demo line is worked out from what that agreement still owes the shop.

**The counter step.** The whole of what still stands on the agreement, namely the hire rate and the add-ons raised on it together with the shop fees and the assessments raised on it, less the money already collected against it, is taken at the counter.

**Resort credit.** Nothing is set against what is taken from resort credit standing on the household's pass account.

**Goodwill.** Nothing is written off for the shop's own part in the hire.

**The security hold.** Nothing is left standing against the security hold.

**How the three meet the counter figure.** The credit set against what is taken, the allowance written off and the amount left standing against the hold are three amounts in money rather than shares of anything, and each is taken off the figure the counter step arrived at rather than off what another of the three has already left.

**The amount.** The amount the guest is asked to hand over is what is left once all three are taken off, never below zero, and rounded half up to two decimal places at that last step only.

## The working on a hypothetical agreement

Take an agreement whose rental account carries a hire rate and add-ons of 186.00 USD, shop fees of 112.00 USD, assessments of 22.25 USD and no money collected against it.

| Step | Working | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the counter step | 186.00 USD together with 112.00 USD and 22.25 USD, less nothing collected | 320.25 USD |
| resort credit | nothing set against the 320.25 USD | nothing |
| goodwill | nothing written off the 320.25 USD | nothing |
| left standing against the hold | nothing measured against the 320.25 USD | nothing |
| the amount | 320.25 USD less the three, never below zero, rounded half up to two decimal places | 320.25 USD |

Where that same account already carried 100.00 USD of money collected, the counter step would arrive at 220.25 USD and the amount the guest is asked to hand over would be 220.25 USD.

## Points of judgement

**Three amounts in money, one common base.** Each of the three is a figure in money, not a percentage of anything, and each is measured against the figure the counter step arrived at. None is worked out on what another of the three has already left, so the order they are taken off in makes no difference to the total.

**One rounding.** The rounding happens once, at the last step, and not at each of the three.

**An agreement that owes nothing.** The amount the guest is asked to hand over is never below zero.
